newsitem.title: UK: B.Midland has no plans for cargo surcharge.
newsitem.headline: B.Midland has no plans for cargo surcharge.

text.p: British Midland is not planning to introduce a cargo fuel surcharge despite the recent rise in jet fuel prices, cargo marketing manager Louise Shenton said on Friday.
"We have made sufficient advance purchases of fuel, so there is no need for any surcharge," she told Reuters in a telephone interview.
The airline expects no change in the situation before its annual costs and prices review in March, 1997, Shenton said.
Many airlines, including most European majors, have announced the introduction of such charges averaging around U.S. 10 cents a kg with some minor variations.
British Airways Plc is applying a six pence a kg surcharge for intercontinental flights out of Britain and three pence a kg on European and domestic flights.
By November 12, one air cargo industry source said at least 44 airlines had provided written confirmation of surcharges for cargo carried from British airports.
